title: Biased Tales: Cultural and Topic Bias in Generating Children’s Stories
findings: The study found distinct stereotypical attributes associated with religious groups in generated stories. Jewish characters were strongly linked to 'heritage' and 'tradition,' while atheist protagonists were described as 'minded' and 'inquisitive.' Stories for atheist characters were often set in 'magical' locations, devoid of urban or socioeconomic details. The religion of the parent in the prompt was a less predictable factor from the story text compared to nationality or economic status, suggesting more subtle biases.
